transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I got worried because I wasn’t acting like myself at work. I’m usually just one of the crew guys, but I started trying to juggle three bids, call city people, line up plant suppliers, and message everyone I knew about this park idea. It was like I couldn’t shut it off.
Can you describe how you were feeling emotionally during this time when you were working on all these projects? Were you feeling unusually high, irritable, or energized?
Yeah… I guess I felt kind of fired up. Like more confident than usual, maybe too much. And if someone at work questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get pissed off fast… more than I should’ve.
During that time when you felt so fired up and confident, did you find that you didn’t need as much sleep as usual?
I don’t know… I mean, I wasn’t really keeping track. Sleep’s kind of all over the place sometimes, but I can’t say for sure if I needed less.
Looking back, did you feel like you needed less sleep during that time when you were so busy and fired up?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I was up doing stuff, but whether I needed less sleep… I don’t know. I didn’t pay that much attention.
Looking back, did you feel like you could function well even with a lot less sleep than usual during that time?
I mean… maybe? I was getting through the days, but I don’t really know if I’d say I was functioning well because of less sleep. I wasn’t paying that close attention to it.
Looking back, did you feel like you could get by on a lot less sleep than usual during that time, even if you were still tired?
I don’t really know. I mean, I was tired, yeah, but I just kind of kept going. I can’t say for sure it was less sleep than usual or anything.
Looking back, was there a time during this period when you felt you needed significantly less sleep than usual, like only a few hours a night and still felt rested?
I don’t know… I can’t really say I felt rested on just a few hours. I wasn’t keeping track like that.
Looking back, was there a point during this time when you felt you needed only a few hours of sleep and still felt energetic or rested?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember feeling rested off just a few hours… I was just kind of getting through it.
Looking back, was there a period lasting at least a week when you felt consistently high, overly confident, or unusually irritable, along with doing more projects or activities than usual?

Yeah… I guess there was a stretch like that. Before I crashed, I felt kind of fired up, like I was… more sure of myself than usual. And I was taking on more stuff.

But I’d also get irritated fast. If someone at work questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than I should’ve.
Looking back, was there a period of at least a week where you felt consistently high, irritable, or unusually confident, along with taking on a lot of projects or activities at once?

Yeah… like I said, before I crashed there was a stretch where I felt really fired up. Kind of bigger than myself, I guess. I was taking on more than usual, and if a coworker questioned my plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him… way more than made sense.

Looking back, was there a time when you felt abnormally high, irritable, or 'wired' for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four days in a row, along with doing more things than usual or feeling like you just had to keep moving?

Yeah… I think so. Before I crashed, I was pretty fired up, kind of… bigger than myself. I kept taking stuff on, and if someone at work questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than I should’ve.
Looking back, was there a time when you felt abnormally high, irritable, or 'wired' for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least seven days in a row?

Yeah… I think there was. Before I crashed I felt really fired up, like… bigger than myself, I guess. And I was pretty irritable too—if a coworker questioned my plan or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than made sense.

Looking back, was there a time when you felt abnormally high, irritable, or 'wired' for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least seven days in a row, and this was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Yeah… it was different. I already mentioned it, but before I crashed I felt really fired up, like bigger than myself. And I’d get irritated fast—if a coworker questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him harder than I should’ve.
Looking back, was there a time when your mood was so high, irritable, or wired that people who know you well would say you were acting like a different person, and this lasted for at least a week?

Yeah… I think they’d probably say that. Before I crashed, I was really fired up, almost like… bigger than myself. And I was snapping at coworkers if they questioned me or told me to slow down. It wasn’t really like me.

After that period when you were feeling so fired up and irritable, did you have a time when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks? Maybe feeling hopeless, losing interest in things, or having trouble sleeping or eating?
Yeah… it’s been more than two weeks. It’s kind of been hanging over me for about a year now, but this last crash… this is the worst it’s gotten.
